nodes.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$ some finite set $P$ of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for $n$-vertex planar graphs: every straight-line planar simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding with all its vertices in $P$.
nodes.title: Planar graphs have subquadratic universal point sets

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$ some finite set of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for $n$-vertex planar graphs.
nodes.title: Subquadratic universal point sets

nodes.summary: A map $p$ from the vertex set of a simple graph $G$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a crossing-free straight-line embedding of $G$ if $p$ is injective, the closed segments $[p(u), p(v)]$ and $[p(x), p(y)]$ of any two different edges $uv$ and $xy$ meet only in points $p(z)$ with $z$ an endpoint of both edges, and no vertex $w$ other than $u$ and $v$ has $p(w)$ on the segment $[p(u), p(v)]$ of an edge $uv$.
nodes.title: Straight-line planar embedding

nodes.summary: A finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is universal for $n$-vertex planar graphs if every straight-line planar simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding $p$ with $p(v) \in P$ for every vertex $v$.
nodes.title: Universal point set for planar graphs
